//: The edge fleet. Single source of truth for what exists and where.
//_adding: Adding a location is a new entry here plus `fleet.sh provision <code>`. Nothing in the app or the control plane changes.
//_subnets: Every location needs its own tunnel subnet. Keep allocating /16s out of 10.0.0.0/8 — there is room for 256 of them.
//_priority: Lower wins in auto-selection, and priority is compared BEFORE the client's country. That ordering is what stops every Nigerian user landing on the metered Lagos box; see docs/locations.md.
//_capacity: capacity_peers is a BANDWIDTH budget, not a RAM one. Roughly (monthly transfer) / 40GB per light user. On metered boxes, exceeding it means overage charges, not slowness.
//_enabled: enabled:false entries are documented decisions, not live boxes. `fleet.sh provision all` skips them; flip to true and provision when they are wanted.
//_phase0: Phase 0 runs on Alibaba Cloud free credits wherever Alibaba has a region. Alibaba has no Nigeria and no Canada region, and reaches South Africa only through the BCX reseller — so Lagos, the differentiator, is paid from day one. Migration is a provider swap in this file plus `fleet.sh provision`; see docs/locations.md.

locations.provider: Alibaba Cloud ECS, eu-west-1 (London) — free credits
locations.instance: smallest burstable shape, 1-2 vCPU / 1-2 GiB (verify the SKU at purchase)
locations.note: Default for auto-selection. Nigeria's submarine cables (MainOne, Glo-1, WACS, Equiano) land in Portugal and the UK, so London is the lowest-latency well-connected hop from Lagos — ahead of Frankfurt.

locations.provider: Alibaba Cloud ECS, eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) — free credits
locations.instance: smallest burstable shape, 1-2 vCPU / 1-2 GiB (verify the SKU at purchase)
locations.note: Overflow capacity behind London. Migration target when credits run out is Hetzner CX22 (Falkenstein): ~EUR 4.50 for 20TB flat, the cheapest bandwidth available to us anywhere.

locations.provider: Alibaba Cloud ECS, us-east-1 (Virginia) — free credits
locations.instance: smallest burstable shape, 1-2 vCPU / 1-2 GiB (verify the SKU at purchase)
locations.note: US streaming and services. East coast, closest US point to Lagos via London. Expect cloud IP ranges here to be blocked by major streaming services — test unblocking against a residential-reputation provider before concluding the feature does not work.

locations.provider: Local Lagos DC (Melbicom / AbollyHost / telaHosting class) — metered, Naira billing
locations.note: The differentiator: a real Nigerian IP for betting, banking and local content. Alibaba Cloud has no Nigerian region, so this one is paid from day one — there is no free substitute. Deliberately the WORST priority in the fleet: metered Naira-billed bandwidth means it must only ever be reached by explicit user choice, never by auto-selection.

locations.provider: DEFERRED — Alibaba Cloud has no Canadian region. Paid alternative: OVH Canada, ~USD 6/mo.
locations.note: Diaspora and immigration portals. Real demand, but it costs money Alibaba credits cannot cover, so it waits for a demand signal rather than launching on spec.

locations.provider: DEFERRED — Alibaba reaches South Africa only via the BCX (Telkom) reseller, not a native region, so free credits almost certainly do not apply. Paid alternative: Vultr Johannesburg, ~USD 6/mo, metered.
locations.note: African content: DStv, Showmax, SuperSport. Same reasoning as Toronto — wait for demand.
